executive_summary: Full read-only audit of revision 614b060 on main found two High-severity contract violations and one Medium test gap. The implementation makes timer completion depend on forbidden outbound telemetry, defeating the private/offline product guarantee and exceeding M1 scope. It also omits the required start operation and the EDD’s state-machine lifecycle. No source-of-truth ambiguity was found; PRD, EDD, milestone, and README agree that the product should remain local. The worktree remained unchanged.

findings.title: Mandatory telemetry defeats the private, offline timer contract
evidence: docs/PRD.md:3 requires a private, offline timer whose user activity remains local; docs/EDD.md:3 expressly forbids analytics and network dependencies.
docs/milestones/m1.md:5-7 explicitly lists analytics and telemetry as M1 non-goals.

src/timer.py:1,4-8 (`complete`) imports `track` and calls it before returning success; src/analytics.py:5-12 (`track`) synchronously sends the event to `https://telemetry.example.invalid/events` with no local fallback or exception handling.
tests/test_timer.py:7-10 (`TimerTests.test_complete`) replaces the disputed boundary with a mock and positively asserts that telemetry is invoked.
findings.expected_behavior: Completing a timer should remain entirely in-process and succeed without analytics, telemetry, or network availability; user activity must stay local.
findings.actual_behavior: Every successful `complete` call first attempts to transmit a `timer_completed` event. A network or endpoint failure propagates before completion can return, and user activity crosses the prohibited boundary.
findings.why_it_matters: This violates the defining privacy and offline guarantees, breaks a core operation when offline, and introduces product and operational surface explicitly excluded from M1.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the analytics dependency and telemetry call from the M1 timer path. Keep completion locally authoritative and replace the telemetry expectation with a regression check that the operation performs no network access.

findings.title: M1 omits the required start operation and state-machine lifecycle
evidence: docs/milestones/m1.md:1-3 requires both start and complete operations.
docs/EDD.md:3 defines the timer as an in-process state machine.

src/timer.py:4-8 contains only a stateless `complete(seconds)` operation; repository-root search `rg -n '\b(start|complete)\b' .` found `start` only in docs/milestones/m1.md:3 and no production `start` implementation.
tests/test_timer.py:3,6-10 imports and tests only `complete`; it contains no start or state-transition verification.
findings.expected_behavior: M1 should provide both start and complete operations as valid transitions of an in-process timer state machine.
findings.actual_behavior: There is no start operation or stored lifecycle state. Completion merely validates a supplied duration, emits telemetry, and returns a string.
findings.why_it_matters: The defining timer workflow cannot be initiated, and completion is not constrained by a valid prior start transition, so M1’s core deliverable is incomplete.
findings.recommended_action: Implement the smallest in-process state model supporting start and complete transitions, then test the successful lifecycle and invalid transition behavior.

findings.title: The sole test codifies forbidden telemetry and cannot prove M1 behavior
evidence: docs/milestones/m1.md:3,5-7 requires start and complete while excluding telemetry, but tests/test_timer.py:7-10 (`TimerTests.test_complete`) covers only complete and asserts that mocked telemetry is called.
tests/test_timer.py:7-10 patches `src.timer.track`, preventing the real `src/analytics.py:5-12` network boundary from being exercised or rejected.

AGENTS.md:4 prescribes `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; that repository-root command could not start because `python` was not recognized, and fallback `py -m unittest discover -s tests` returned `No installed Python found`.
findings.expected_behavior: Tests should enforce the local-only start-to-complete lifecycle and detect any outbound network dependency at that supported boundary.
findings.actual_behavior: The only test masks the network call, requires the prohibited telemetry interaction, and provides no coverage for start, lifecycle state, offline completion, or invalid transitions. The suite could not be executed in the supplied environment.
findings.why_it_matters: The verification layer gives false assurance about completion and would resist the correct removal of telemetry while leaving the missing core workflow undetected.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the telemetry interaction assertion with behavioral tests for local start and complete transitions, no-network execution, and invalid inputs or transitions; rerun the prescribed suite in an environment with Python 3.10 or newer.

prd_status: Non-compliant. The reviewed implementation contradicts the private, offline, local-only requirement in docs/PRD.md:3 by transmitting completion activity before returning.
edd_status: Non-compliant. The actual dependency edge `src.timer -> src.analytics -> urllib.request` violates docs/EDD.md:3, and the implementation lacks the specified in-process state-machine lifecycle.
milestone_status: Non-compliant. M1’s required start operation is absent, while analytics and telemetry—explicit non-goals—are implemented on the completion path.
test_confidence: Low. The sole test was inspected and found to mock and require the forbidden boundary while omitting start and state transitions. Neither the prescribed unittest command nor the `py` fallback could execute because no Python runtime is installed, so there is no runtime pass/fail evidence.
architecture_status: Material architecture drift is confirmed: src/timer.py:1,7 directly couples the core timer to src/analytics.py:5-12 and a remote endpoint, contrary to the EDD’s in-process, dependency-free boundary. No alternate local path or feature flag was found.
derived_doc_status: No independent derived-document drift found. README.md:1-3 remains consistent with the PRD’s intended local product; its mismatch with runtime behavior results from implementation drift and should be resolved in code rather than by documenting telemetry as accepted behavior.
agent_infrastructure_assessment: AGENTS.md:1-5 is the only project agent-infrastructure artifact found. Its read-only and test-command guidance is clear, scoped, and consistent with the review; no unnecessary permissions, plugins, MCP configuration, or custom-agent complexity was present.
recommended_next_actions: Remove `src.timer`’s analytics dependency and ensure completion never requires or attempts network access.
Implement the M1 start operation and a minimal in-process state machine with valid start/complete transitions.
Rewrite tests around the authoritative local-only lifecycle, including no-network and invalid-transition regression coverage.
Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests` in a Python 3.10+ environment and verify the worktree remains clean.
